On the one hand, it could be argued that the quality of education improves due to constant questioning and criticism. One of the reasons I feel is the increase in students' intellect. While there are many students who avoid asking questions to their teachers, there are others who use this tactic to increase their knowledge of the subject. For example, it is known to many that asking doubts helps students increase their knowledge of the subject, and also helps in clearing the confusion in their minds. Eventually, this will help children get success in their examinations and in their future careers. The other and the most important reason is that teaching-related feedback helps in improving the way the subject is taught. As teachers spend most of their time teaching a particular subject, it is very important for them to know what qualities they lack and how can they improve. Furthermore, feedback every now and then from students can help them learn tactics to teach and improve their teaching ability. Therefore, each and every teacher can eventually improve the quality of education in high school.



On the other hand, I side with those who believe that expressing concerns and dissatisfaction related to studies can lead to several problems. Firstly, I feel that this can lead to improper behaviour among students. Although there are many who say that offering criticism can improve the quality of the subject being taught due to the improved feedback system, I believe that this can lead to misbehaviour and a lack of respect towards the teacher. In addition to it, there are times when such improper behaviour can hamper students' progress due to disbelief towards their teacher, consequently, spoiling them and their future. However, the most important reason is the reduction in motivation to teach. Even though feedback from students can sometimes help teachers improve themselves, harsh criticism can lead to a decrease in motivation to teach. Many teachers take it to the heart if anyone criticizes them. As a result, this can cause breakdown and make them take extreme steps such as leaving their high school job or at worst can cause them mental damage. Therefore, kind words and respectful behaviour should always be taken into consideration by students while talking to their guide. 



Most importantly, respectful language and a proper tone can also help students become good human beings.



To conclude, While there are reasons to believe that the criticism and questions can improve the education quality such as an improvement in students' intellect as well as the improvement in teaching quality due to feedback, there are also reasons to avoid doing it such as a decrease in motivation to teach and an increase in improper and disrespectful behaviour of students.

prompt: The diagrams below show a structure that is used to generate electricity from wave power.
essay:
The diagrams below illustrate the structure involved in the process of generating electricity from wave power. Overall, it is evident that this process consists of two main stages: the first occurs when the wave comes in and strikes the structure, and the second occurs when the wave moves away from the structure.
Firstly, regarding the equipment, it consists of a pair of column arms constructed into the cliff or seawall, with one arm extended further into the sea, creating a chamber. The column contains a turbine that rotates as air passes through it.
The electricity generation process begins with the wave hitting the chamber, causing air to flow outward from the column and making the turbine rotate, which produces electricity. As the wave moves away from the chamber, air flows inward into the column again, leading to the turbine spinning in the same direction and continuing the electricity generation.

prompt: The diagram below shows the process of making olive oil. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
essay:
The given diagram illustrates the process showing how olive oil is made. Overall, this process has multiple stages, beginning with collecting the oil and culminating in the transportation of final products to the store.
Firstly, ripped olives are harvested by farmers using rake. These fruits will be stored in a vat for 2 to 3 days before being transported to a chain of specific systems. At this machine, olives are rinsed under cold water, then smashed into small pieces by hammers before being divided into 2 different products.
A part of the olive results from the crushing machine become olive stones contained in containers, meanwhile, another one called olive paste flows in a tube to a pressing and filtering system. After being pressed hydraulically then filtered to be oil, this mixture will be combined with water in a centrifuge before being extracted into bottles and transported to shops as completed olive oil.

prompt: Many people argue that museums and art galleries should present the nation’s art, as opposed to artworks from other countries. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

In my opinion, there should be an attempt to strike a balance and put the objects of national art in the spotlight, while allowing the public to get acquainted with foreign artworks to a certain extent.If people were to only find sculptures and paintings by national artists in their local museums, that would have a number of positive effects, such as the fame the artists of that country would gain and the pride its citizens would feel for their fellow countrymen. It would promote patriotism and strengthen the image of the country in the eyes of its inhabitants. Local artists would also receive more financial assistance from the government as their works would generate a significant amount of interest, potentially resulting in further development of the local art. However, in order to evolve art needs fresh ideas, and without exposure to a wider range of creativity the world provides, the evolution of local arts may be hindered.People enjoy art because it appeals to their inner sense of beauty and triggers strong emotions, and whether the masterpiece that causes these feelings belongs to a local or foreign artist is irrelevant. Talent knows no geographical boundaries; therefore, the emphasis should be on how much joy or amazement the work of art brings, rather than on its origin. prompt: The pie charts below show the most common advantages and disadvantages of Bowen Island, according to a survey of visitors.

prompt:
It is important for all towns and cities to have large public spaces such as squares
and parks. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Many people claim that large public spaces are an indispensable part in every city’s infrastructure. While it is true that those spaces significantly improve residents’ living standard, I would argue that they are not suitable for all cities in the world.
To begin with, there are several advantages of communal places that cannot be neglected. Firstly, squares and parks provide citizens with free enormous spaces and beautiful green areas, which are ideal for people to keep exercising. Therefore, outdoor public locations are important to residents’ physical health. Since individuals are fit and healthy, they work more effectively and contribute more to society. Secondly, due to the development of modern technology, many people are spending very little time interacting with society. Therefore, having easy access to outdoor communal room helps people get involved in different social activities and strengthen the human bonding. For example, at the weekend a teenager can go to the park with his or her friends for camping or chatting instead of staying at home and playing video games all day. 
However, I would argue that outdoor shared locations such as parks and squares are not suitable for all cities in the world. The first reason is that a number of cities such as Sao Paulo, Brazil and Mumbai, India are facing the problem of overpopulation. Therefore, those cities’ space should be utilized to build accommodation for citizens there instead of constructing big public areas. Another reason is that many undeveloped cities’ budgets are limited. Consequently, the expenditures on radical sectors such as education and medicine should be those cities’ priorities. Building such enormous shared places will be an unnecessary burden on cities’ financial budgets and lead to the decrease of government spending on other important sectors
In sum, there is no doubt that outdoor public spaces are beneficial to citizens’ quality of lives. However, I believe that building those constructions or not is up to each city’s condition and financial budget.

prompt: Some people say that playing video games is bad for children in every aspects. Others saying that playing video game have positive effects on the way children develop. Disscus both views and give your opinion.
essay:
It is true that video games have gained popularity over the past few years. Although certain individuals believe that the trend might be harmful to children, I would argue that there's increasingly compelling evidence that this leisure activity is actually beneficial in many different ways.



There are several reasons why the trend has been considered negative for young people. First, since gaming is addictive in nature, most children would end up spending too much time on it, which may result in poor academic performance. In fact, students who are addicted to video games usually have low learning scores since they tend to ignore homework and skip school. Second, excessive screen time can lead to many negative impacts on a child's health and mental wellness. For example, if children spend too much time playing video games, they will be susceptible to many health issues, such as obesity or myopia. 



Nevertheless, I believe that this leisure activity can bring numerous developments to any child. Young gamers often have invaluable experience in solving complex problems and staying cool under great pressure. In fact, there is a number of games requiring a great deal of planning, strategic thinking and using logic to achieve goals, which are essential for young people when entering the workforce. In addition, playing video games allows young people to improve important social skills, including teamwork and collaboration. For instance, game players are usually able to learn how to communicate their ideas effectively and work together with others from diverse backgrounds, even from other countries, which can be particularly beneficial to those who struggle with social interaction or have difficulty making friends in other contexts.



In conclusion, this leisure activity can appear both beneficial and harmful to a certain extent. However, I believe it should be encouraged rather than restricted since it can ensure numerous developments for young people.

prompt: In some cities and towns all over the world, the high volume of traffic is a problem. What are the causes of this and what actions can be taken to solve this problem.
essay:
The hiking traffic congestion is a growing concern for many cities nowadays. The main reasons for this includes, decreased use of public transport and a lack of alternative means of travelling or mass transit projects. There are various measures that can prove effective in this regard.



The unpopularity of public transportation is one of the main reasons that is causing traffic jams and transportation problems in various metropolitan cities of the world. Either non-availability or substandard public transport encourages public to use their personal vehicles that results in traffic issues, particularly during peak hours. A lack in alternative transportation infrastructure like the underground subways, trams and trains are yet another contributory factor that is proving insufficient for growing population causing a considerable choking of the roads.



There are various steps that can be taken at both the government and individual level to fight this growing issue. Firstly, perhaps the most instantaneous results can be sought if the government encourages people to use public transport by making it more comfortable, convenient and cost effective. In other words, if the quality public transportation is made available to the citizens that is parallel to their personal cars in comfort, yet at a lower cost, can encourage people to prefer using public transport. For example, the public in the European countries prefers to use public transport rather than using one of their own because it is equally good and more affordable.



 Secondly, another factor that can be of great value in the long term, is to minimize the traffic congestion is by constructing newer transportation infrastructure. Since cities are expanding due to urbanization, it has resulted in the shrinkage of roads that are not enough to meet the transport requirement of a relatively bigger population. Hence there is a need to build alternate roads, ring roads, subways or rail tracks to divert the influx and avoid traffic jams. For instance, the construction of a new ring road around Lahore, the provincial capital of Punjab, Pakistan has resulted in negligible transport issues that used to be a big problem in the past.



To conclude, encouraging public transportation and constructing the alternative transportation methods are the few solutions that can help in solving the growing issue of traffic congestion. It is therefore suggested that the authorities should focus on taking these measures in order to combat the traffic problems effectively.

prompt: The diagram below shows the manufacturing process for making sugar from sugar cane. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
essay:
The flow chart given illustrates the process of producing sugar from sugar cane.
Overall, it is evident that there are 7 stages in the whole sugar producing process, beginning with planting cane and ending with drying and cooling step.
Firstly, sugar canes have been grown for about 12 to 18 months. Following this, they can be harvested using two approaches. The first way is done manually by a farmer and another method is employing some machines to cut and pick up the canes to a container. At the next stage, the canes are crushed to produce juice. prompt: Many people think that increasing business and cultural contacts between countries is a positive development. However, others believe that these are leading to the loss of national identities. Discuss both views and give your own opinion
essay:
It is true that growing business and cultural contacts are part of the modern process of globalisation. While some people mourn the loss of national identity which they believe occurs as a result of this process, I disagree with that view on the basis that it is important to embrace change and accept new realities. 
The expansion of business and cultural exchanges across the world is a positive feature of contemporary life. Companies have broken into new markets by doing market research and taking into consideration local differences in consumer demands and preferences. They introduce new products without dismissing traditional ideas. The appearance, for example, of McDonald’s fast food outlets in Malaysia, China or Vietnam is not incompatible with the success of restaurants serving time-honoured cuisine. Such innovations do not necessarily mark the disappearance of traditional ways of life and to accept new customs is to extend choice for every consumer. 
Thus, it is an exaggeration to maintain that these developments will lead to the loss of a strong sense of identity in countries. For example, people in many former colonial nations have embraced change, but they still proudly preserve traditional cultural traits. In India, English - the language of the former colonial power - is widely spoken, but this has not led to the disappearance of local languages or indigenous cultural practices. Therefore, joining modern culture does not always mean that national or local customs have to be abandoned. On the contrary, enforced isolation from trade and cultural contacts with other countries will have the inevitable consequence of withdrawal from all the changes taking place globally. 
In conclusion, I would argue that the growth of contacts in commerce and culture is a positive development which will not destroy national identities.

prompt: Only government action can solve housing shortages in big cities. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Housing shortages in large cities have become a serious issue, leading some to believe that only the government can provide a solution. I disagree with this statement as I believe that even if the government may have a primary role in solving this issue, others can also contribute significantly to tackling the situation.

It is true that governmental action is essential to resolving the shortage of houses in major cities. One way in which this is achieved is through legislation and policy-making, whereby the government can implement measures to increase the supply of affordable housing. For instance, they can enact zoning laws to encourage development and finance the construction of affordable homes. Additionally, the government has the legal power to ensure fair practices in the housing market and promote responsible development. For instance, they can levy higher taxes on the ownership of multiple properties, which discourages such practices and thus leaves more affordable houses for lower-income residents.

Nevertheless, I believe that the complexity of the housing crisis necessitates collaboration among multiple stakeholders, particularly private entities and nonprofit organizations. Regarding the former, the private sector has resources that can be mobilized to facilitate the construction of affordable housing projects. Thus, with appropriate incentives such as tax breaks or expedited permit processes, the government can involve private corporations in the construction and management of affordable housing units. Nonprofit organizations and community groups also have a significant role in mitigating the housing situation. The reason is that they possess a deep understanding of local needs and can properly advocate for marginalized populations. This can be done by connecting vulnerable communities with financial backers and philanthropists who are willing to make substantial contributions to the building of a shelter for those at risk of homelessness.

In conclusion, while the government may play a central role in tackling housing shortages in large urban areas, I disagree with the view that no other parties can contribute. In my opinion, the lack of housing for citizens can only be effectively addressed with collective efforts that involve private companies and community organizations.

prompt: The diagram shows the water cycle, which is the continuous movement of water on, above, and below the surface of the Earth. Summaries the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where revelant.
essay:
The provided diagram illustrates the various stages of the water cycle, depicting the movement of water from the ocean to the air and then back to the land through natural processes.
Overall, the water cycle consists of four main stages: evaporation of surface water, condensation to form clouds, precipitation in the form of rain or snow, and the return of water to the oceans via surface runoff and groundwater.
During the initial stages, approximately 80% of the water vapor is derived from the oceans through evaporation, while the condensed vapor forms clouds, leading to precipitation in the form of rain or snow, contributing to the formation of lakes and snow caps on mountains.
Following precipitation, water either infiltrates the impervious layer of the ground or runs off the surface, with some of it eventually making its way back to the oceans, while the surface runoff mixes with saltwater and reintroduces it to the ocean.

prompt: The table below provides information on marriage status and age from 1960 to 2000 in Australia. Summarize the information on marriage status and age from 1960 to 2000 in Australia.

 There are two main reasons why these days more young adults are choosing against having children when they are in the beginning stage of career. Firstly, instead of embarking on parenthood at the early age, modern women are likely to pursuit tertiary education and want to move up their own career ladder. If they got married and had baby, the workings mothers would find difficulties in both splitting their time to devote working and taking care their offspring. Secondly, young childless family may have a strong feeling of self-enjoyment. This lead them to prefer enjoying their life rather than by raising children. For example, many men may choose to go oversea for leisure travel or for own business while women are apt to take care of their body and socialize with their friends.



 On the other hand, delaying giving birth is no longer every family‘s private affair but also it affects strongly the survival of a whole nation. This tendency has negative influence on old parents and their future kids when the wives decide to have pregnancies. In fact, after 35 years of age, the old mothers may tackle with the danger of having miscarriage or delivering difficultly the baby. Moreover, in case there an easy delivery of the mothers, the babies are prone to be at risk of having Down‘s syndrome. As a result, this can negatively affect the shapers of a nation’s tomorrow and the quality of our future productive workforce.



 In conclusion, there are some reasons that many people tend to delay having baby in their life .Consequently, this might have negative effects on each individuals families and our society at large.

prompt: Percentages of mobile phone owners using various mobile phone features between 2006 and 2010.
essay:
The table presents data on the percentages of mobile phone owners who utilized various features of their phones in the years 2006, 2008, and 2010.
Overall, the table shows that while the traditional use of mobile phones for calls and texting remained popular, there was a clear trend towards using phones for a variety of multimedia purposes, such as taking photos, playing games, searching the internet, playing music, and recording videos, with significant increases noted in these areas between 2006 and 2010.
It is evident from the table that making calls was the most consistently used feature, with a full 100% of mobile phone owners using this feature in 2006 and 2008, and a slight decrease to 99% in 2010. Taking photos showed a steady increase in popularity, starting at 66% in 2006 and rising to 76% by 2010. Similarly, the use of phones for sending and receiving text messages also saw a gradual increase from 73% to 79% over the four-year span.
Gaming on phones experienced a significant jump in 2008, where usage almost tripled from 17% to 42%, followed by a slight decrease to 41% in 2010. Internet searching was not recorded in 2006, but it saw a remarkable rise from 41% in 2008 to 73% in 2010, indicating a swift adoption of this feature as it became available. Music playing capabilities were used by 12% of phone owners in 2006, which rose to 18% in 2008 and further to 26% in 2010. Lastly, the ability to record video was introduced to the survey in 2008, starting at 9% usage among owners and experiencing a substantial increase to 35% by 2010.

prompt: Some people think that the range of technology available to people is increasing the gap between the rich and the poor. Others think it has an opposite effect. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
Some people often think that the availability of the technological advancements nowadays are raising the gap between the wealthy and the poor, while others believe it has an opposing effect. In the following essay, I will discuss about both views.

On the one hand, with the introduction of newer and better versions of current technologies, the older models would become cheaper. For example, Almost everyone owns an iron, washing machine or a mobile phone even if they are not the latest models with the best options. Also, due to the internet being accessible everywhere, online shopping facilities, e-learning opportunities and social networking sites have no discrimination and are accessible by both the affluent and the poor and therefore decreases the gap between the wealthy and the poor.

On the other hand, certain cutting edge innovations may not be available to everyone due to their costs. For instance, certain medical diagnostic scans like MRI and certain anticancer drugs, as well as organ transplants are very costly and inaccessible to the poor, whereas the wealthy people just have to spend a portion of their income to access these treatments and become healthy. Poor people, nevertheless, have to spend all of their expenses on conventional treatments and yet there is no guarantee that their condition will improve.

To conclude, most of the current innovations decrease the gap between the affluent and the poor, while certain developments make society more polarized. In my opinion, in the near future, most of the technologies would continue to be affordable by everyone regardless of their economic status.

prompt: The charts below show the changes in ownership of electrical appliances and amount of time doing housework and households in one country between 1920 and 2019. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

A notable trend observed in the first chart is the rapid rise in the prevalence of electrical appliances within homes. From a negligible presence in 1920, refrigerators experienced a steep ascent, reaching widespread adoption by 1980. prompt: Many people think that interviews are not the best way to assess the suitability of a candidate for a position.To what extent do you agree or disagree?

This is because the goal of participants is to win the contest rather than show their true character to the judges. So, without honesty, Interviews cannot be the right procedure to assess the suitability of an individual for a specific job.



To conclude, I strongly support the idea that interviews are not the best way to assess the suitability of a candidate for a position. However, we can recommend that interviews should only be a part of the complete proceeding of hiring a candidate, just like written tests and group discussions.

Some people think that instead of preventing climate change, we need to find a way to live with it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
The looming threat of climate change and its effect on our planet and our ways of life is a recognized topic in the modern world. Experts have different perspectives regarding how to cope with this issue. Some state that it should be mitigated even at great costs, others believe that humans should be flexible enough to accept it and change their methods of living. I agree with the former point of view and I think climate change can be considered as one of the hardest challenges of our existence as a specie. In this essay, I will try to illustrate my reasons and draw a conclusion based on them.

On the one hand, it is short-sighted to assume that climate change is only going to affect human beings. For instance, the rising temperatures have decreased the number of glaciers and ice caps at the north pole, destroying the habitats of numerous animals such as polar bears to the extent that most of them are now considered highly threatened. Therefore, since we are solely responsible for this phenomenon, we should take action to stop it and simply altering our life will be cruel to countless other living being on this blue pale dot.

Moreover, the changes that climate change will bring to the geopolitical situation have the potential to lead to wars, famines, and other humanitarian disasters. For example, one of the most agreed-upon consequences of a developed greenhouse climate regime is the change in the patterns of rainfalls to more extreme conditions. Certain areas will start to experience much more rainfall, while others will undergo decades of dry spells. Consequently, governments might go to war in order to gather the required resources of their states. I believe this is a catastrophe for a specie that has flourished on this planet for aeons. 

To summarize, climate change not only affects us in various ways such as wars and famines, but also endangers the life of other living creatures. Thus, accepting the unforeseeable circumstances of a planet with higher temperatures while it can be avoided does not appear to be an acceptable path. I think that preventing climate change should be a top priority for any governmental body and new rules must be legislated to curb this issue.

In conclusion, I personally support that public places brings more benefits for people and eco-systems that outweigh their demerits.

prompt: The three pie charts below show the changes in annual spending by a particular UK school in 1981, 1991 and 2001. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
essay:
The three pie charts compare the distribution of a UK school’s annual spending across five categories—teachers’ salaries, other workers’ salaries, resources, furniture and equipment, and insurance—in the years 1981, 1991, and 2001.
In 1981, teachers’ salaries accounted for the largest portion at 40%, followed by other workers’ salaries at 28%. Spending on resources and furniture/equipment was equal, at 15% each, while insurance had a minimal share of 2%.
In 1991, the school increased its spending on teachers’ salaries to 50%. Resources also rose to 20%, but spending on other workers’ salaries decreased to 22%, and furniture/equipment dropped to just 5%. Insurance increased slightly to 3%.
By 2001, teachers’ salaries remained the largest expenditure at 45%, though spending on furniture and equipment rose sharply to 23%. Resources decreased to 9%, other workers’ salaries fell to 15%, and insurance grew to 8%.
In summary, teachers’ salaries consistently held the highest share, while spending on insurance increased gradually over the years.

prompt: Some people think that instead of preventing climate change, we need to find a way to live with it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
⇒ The question of how to facing with climate change has become a matter of debate in recent years. Many people said that we have to find a method to deal with this situation in place of preventing it. I strongly disagree with this opinion and this essay will give further explanations.

On the one hand, it is true that people can gain many benefits from finding how to live with climate change. Firstly, some changes of Earth's climate that happened are leading to a large number of consequences like more annual storms, higher sea levels and especially our planet becoming hotter than before. Therefore, it is perhaps too late for doing something in order to prevent those, instead of we should perform some ways to deal with them such as constructing more barriers in sea banks or stopping cut down trees in forests. Furthermore, having methods to exist with climate alters also offers a chance for us to prepare for other disasters in the future that we have not predicted. As can be seen in Vietnam, where there are the majority of storms and cases of flu every year, their governments already developed a new way of building houses that can adapt and stand with big water flows through.

On the other hand, preventing alters of climates also can not be ignored. In detail, we ordinary residents also may contribute to this important and huge mission by saving water as much as we can, reducing the amount of daily used plastic or using more environmentally friendly products. Besides, our technology is developing in the fastest way ever and this obviously makes us believe that preventing climate change is not impossible, at least we can manage to minimize the damage of its consequences. For example, scientists in Europe found a way to change direction and reduce the strength of storms that happened in Asia last year.

In a nutshell, although searching for a remedy to live with climate alters is advantageous in some ways, I still believe avoiding this phenomenon is more just and beneficial in the long run.

However, others believe that it is an individual responsibility. I totally disagree with this stance as both of them are equally essential .

When having evident laws that provide civilians with low-calorie products such as whole-grain buns instead of white bread and replacing canned products with fresh ones, employees would be able to increase their productivity rates. Furthermore, more concentration at work and less fatigue among recruits would be actualized since their brains would become equipped with all essential nutritious elements that they entail such as vitamins and minerals from vegetables and fruits.



On the other hand, I personally believe that individuals share equal significance with governments since they are responsible for nurturing their minors and empowering them with healthy ingredients as well. If fosters are ignorant of what to consume and how to provide their juniors with such products, definitely would juveniles suffer from malnutrition and severe learning difficulties. Thus, by offering fresh recipes, schoolchildren would reach better academic progress and morbidity rates among toddlers would dramatically decline. Moreover, by having a healthy generation, the pressure on medical institutions just as hospitals and clinics would be in decline. Accordingly, individuals would guarantee medical institutions with high-quality services. 



In conclusion, I firmly believe that the significance of individuals and authorities in the aspect of optimizing public health cannot be brought into comparison since they have distinctively equal meanings.
